units: Ex. R. s. 35 א׳ נעשו וכ׳ (Pes. 118ᵇ, corr. acc) they were a lodging place to my children in Egypt (they offered hospitality to &c.).—בעל א׳ host.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 85a:20">B. Mets. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>תורה מחזרת על א׳ שלה</he> scholarship likes to come around to its inn again (to be hereditary in the family); a. fr.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 87a:8">B. Mets. 87ᵃ</cite> one must inquire <he>בא׳ שלו</he> after the health of his hostess.

senses.gloss: quarter given to troops on march or to transient poor men; also the passing troop, or the passing poor; (individ.) beggar.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 31:32">Targ. Job XXXI, 32</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 11b:6">B. Bath. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ לפי בני אדם</he> the quartering (of soldiers takes place) in proportion to the number of inmates (of each house).
<cite ref="Mishnah Demai 3:1">Dem. III, 1</cite>; v. Y. ib. 23ᵇ top.
<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 5:21">Tosef. Shebi. V, 21</cite> <he>אין מאכילין אכסניין וכ׳</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>את אכסניא</he>) you are not allowed to give … to soldiers quartered with you.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:23">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵇ</cite> <he>ההן א׳ עלובתא</he> this poor beggar.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:23">Ib.</cite> <he>א׳ עלו׳</he> poor beggars.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> (<he>חד מירו׳</he>) <he>בר נש א׳</he> a poor man.

senses.gloss: a gathering of scholars entertained by the hospitable of the place.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:4:6">Y. Ber. IV, 8ᵇ</cite> top <he>נפיק לא׳</he> leaving for the scholars’ meeting. Bab.
<cite ref="Berakhot 63b:23">Ber. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>פתח בכבוד א׳</he> opened his speech in honor of hospitality to scholars.
